whoAmI.title: About me...
whoAmI.content2: Since my childhood, I've been fascinated by the world of video games, a passion that sparked my interest in development. I then began my studies in the field of web development to understand development in general, and obtained a Bachelor's degree in Multimedia and Internet Jobs, thus laying a solid foundation for my career.
whoAmI.content3: Currently, I am a student at the IIM Digital School in Paris, focusing on the video game axis, in order to leverage my technical skills and passion for this field that I am so passionate about.
whoAmI.content4: Always eager to broaden my skillset, I approach each challenge with enthusiasm and a commitment to continuous improvement.

opquast.title: Opquast certification
opquast.content: I am also Opquast certified, which is a certification that validates the knowledge of good web practices. This certification is recognized by the French government and is a real asset in the field of web development. I scored 830 points, which corresponds to the advanced level.

description.title: Project Overview
description.content: So’Briquet is an endless scrolling game created in just 4 days for a back-to-school game jam! </br>The main constraint was to integrate a lighter as a constant element of the gameplay. Unexpected twists during development added extra challenges, but they also pushed us to be more creative and refine the project further.

Work.descTask: During this project, I developed player-oriented gameplay mechanics. Throughout the process, I took into account the imposed constraints while also giving the Game Designers the flexibility to adjust key parameters as needed.

projects.name: Frag'Ture
projects.myTasks: Lead Programmer, Gameplay Programmer, UI Programmer

description.title: Project Overview
description.content:
Frag'Ture is a fast-paced local 1v1 FPS developed during my studies at IIM Digital School in Paris. Set in a futuristic arena, two players face off in intense duels where the objective is to secure victory by defeating the opponent three times.
Players must master advanced movement mechanics such as slides and dashes, while also leveraging a unique feature: the time fracture. This mechanic dynamically alters the environment, weapons, and even player movement, offering fresh tactical opportunities throughout the match.
Fast reflexes, adaptability, and strategy are the keys to dominating the arena.

Work.descTask: As Lead Programmer, I was responsible for ensuring the smooth progress of the project from a technical perspective. In addition to contributing to the core programming tasks, I coordinated the team’s workflow, tracked progress, and maintained clear communication between programming and other disciplines (game design, art, audio, etc.).

I developed environmental gameplay mechanics such as bumpers, lava traps, and a map-switching system every 30 seconds.
I designed a collision interface for bumpers, allowing characters to trigger specific interactions. Lava traps were scripted to activate automatically after 5 seconds on the past map.
We leveraged level streaming to dynamically load and unload the two maps, significantly optimizing performance.

I implemented the user interface systems, including menus, scoreboards, timer, and health bars, ensuring proper synchronization between UI elements and game logic. All systems were designed to be easily configurable by designers.
I structured several Widget Blueprints in Unreal Engine, creating reusable and modular components with clean, independent logic to guarantee a clear and scalable UI.

description.title: Description
description.content: Lunacy is a mobile game I developed at IIM Digital School in Paris. In it, you play as the last survivor aboard a doomed spaceship, heading for a crash. Your only hope is to return to the cockpit and regain control of the vessel. To reach it, you'll need to solve puzzles and unlock doors using repair drones, guiding your way toward survival. But as you journey through the ship’s dark corridors, you’ll have to fight off the creeping grip of space madness. Will you save yourself before it’s too late?

Work.descTask:
On this project, I developed several UI behaviors, including menu interactions, a level selector, and battery stock animations.
Since our game is divided into different biomes, we decided to place everything in a single scene to avoid loading times during gameplay.
To make this work, I created a biome manager script in C#, built on a custom save system.

To organize the team as efficiently as possible, we created a documentation with a specific naming convention.
Later on, I set up a Trello board to assign and track tasks for each role.
Knowing who was responsible for what helped us move forward smoothly.

description.title: Description
description.content: Outside of my studies, I tried creating a mod for the first Slime Rancher game. The idea was to add a timer to track how long it takes to open a specific gate. The goal was to compare different runs, improve over time, and record your best time for a speedrun.

Work.descTask: For this mod, I used BepInEx, a piece of software that allows me to write code that the game can read alongside the original developers' code. To manage the timer and related systems, I used Harmony, a library that lets me add patches — a way to listen to events in the original code and trigger actions at specific moments — and Newtonsoft.Json, another library used to read and write JSON files.

description.title: Description
description.content:
Fungi is a small game I developed during Ludum Dare 56, a 3-day game jam with the theme: Tiny Creatures.
The game follows a little mushroom trying to fit into his tribe while helping its members.
However, his journey is challenging due to his differences...

Work.descTask: Since the project lasted 3 days, the main task for the UI was to design the main menu. I made the menu fully controller-compatible by setting the 'Play' button as the default selection and enabling navigation through buttons using controller arrows. Additionally, I displayed control text, integrating the input system configuration to serve as a tutorial for the players.

For this project, I managed the Input System configuration and the gameplay mechanics linked to it. Additionally, I implemented features such as bouncing on mushrooms and creating spore platforms. These platforms spawn slightly above the character's position, allowing him to reach higher areas than with a regular jump.

description.title: Description
description.content: To celebrate the 30th anniversary of the MMI/SRC program, we organized an exceptional event featuring escape rooms, providing our guests with a memorable anniversary evening. For this project, I served as the back-end developer for the WebOdyssey site, the name of our event. I developed an API using NodeJS, which efficiently managed the various event functionalities. Additionally, I implemented a mailing system with NodeMailer to send confirmation emails and entry tickets to the visitors. This approach ensured a smooth and professional experience for all participants.

Work.descTask:
For this project, we built the website’s front-end with NextJS and the back-end with NodeJS and Express.
As a back-end developer, I secured data transfers to the database and made data management easier for the administrator.
A major task was also generating entry tickets on the fly and sending them by email.
I used users’ reservation details to create a PDF ticket and send it directly to them.

To host our website, we used Vercel to maintain NextJS’s dynamic capabilities and to make production updates easier directly through Git.
Then, I updated the domain's DNS settings to properly redirect to Vercel and adjusted some configurations to link O2switch’s mail service with Vercel.

description.title: Description
description.content: As part of a study project, we had the pleasure of creating a mini-game using the Unity engine. To help us achieve this project, we had resource classes to understand the engine and the programming language, which is C#. We were free to choose the theme, the game physics, provided there was a win/lose condition, the use of the Input System, and the use of prefabs. During this project, I wanted to go a step further by learning how to use scriptable objects and Cinemachine, which allowed me to give more life to my game.

description.title: Description
description.content: In December 2024, I had the very special pleasure of participating in the Night of Info. Accompanied by my friends Amézir Messaoud, Amel Chabah, and Driss Benadjal, we created a website on the theme of climate change (which was the theme imposed for this 2024 edition). In addition to the limited time, another constraint for this website was that it had to include a question-answer game. That's when we thought about adding 3D using the ThreeJS library. After 8 hours of hackathon, we delivered our "Planet Danette" website. It won second place for the most accessible website. It's a result we're very proud of, especially considering how complex it is to make a website accessible with 3D.

Work.descTask: As I mentioned earlier, we had to create a small game about climate change on this website. Since we chose to build a 3D website, I was responsible for creating the 3D scene for the game. To assist myself, I used Spline to manage the 3D elements and then exported it into a ThreeJS format to integrate it into the website. I also placed several cameras to focus on the relevant elements for each question. We linked each question to a specific camera, so when you answer a question, the camera switches to focus on the next one.

description.title: Description
description.content: At the end of my second year of MMI, we had to create a website for a fictional art exhibition. We chose to focus on the Impressionist movement because we found it very interesting and thought it would fit well with the concept of the site we had in mind. For this project, I was the interactive developer. My task was to create an augmented reality feature directly accessible from the website! To do this, I used Blender to create a custom scene that I imported as GLTF using the ThreeJS library, allowing me to manage the 3D environment in the browser, and I used WebXR to implement this famous augmented reality feature.

description.title: Description
description.content: At the beginning of my second year of MMI, we were asked to create a data visualization website on a theme of our choice. For this project, I was accompanied by Clara Many and Pagnarith Kok Srey. We chose to address the theme of femicides because we believe it is still too little highlighted despite its importance in society. To populate our site, we retrieved data from the feminicides.fr website, which lists the number of femicides per year since 2016. This impactful project was presented on the Gustave Eiffel University website for the Day against Violence towards Women. It was also mentioned on the list of committed student projects proposed by the Gustave Eiffel University website.

tesimonials.name: Julien Chamayou
tesimonials.comment: I had the opportunity to supervise Noam during his internship within a web application development project at Sopra Steria. Noam is committed, personable, and proactive. He integrated very well into the team and effectively improved his skills over time on a technical stack he was not familiar with (Java, Spring, VueJS) in order to deliver high-quality outcomes, always adhering to the team's processes.

tesimonials.name: Emilien Regent
tesimonials.comment: Noam has shown a real aptitude for the Unity engine. He quickly gained proficiency in the topics covered in class (engine foundation, 3Cs) and didn't hesitate to delve into other concepts on his own (scriptable objects, cinemachine).

tesimonials.name: Amel Chabah
tesimonials.work: UX/UI Designer & Full-Stack Developer at GAEL Systems
tesimonials.comment: Noam is an exceptional collaborator whose bright personality and remarkable skills have left a mark on every project we have shared. Endowed with natural charisma and innate leadership qualities, he inspires everyone to give their best. A born educator, he motivates and guides his team with uncommon ease. His ease with public speaking and relentless commitment make him a true asset to all his projects. Always in pursuit of perfection, Noam embraces challenges with enthusiasm, bringing positive energy to every situation. Working alongside him is a real pleasure, and I am convinced that he will continue to shine and be a source of inspiration for all his future projects.
